topic.title: Nested if and Multi-Way if-else Statements
topic.description: Complex decision making with nested conditions

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
How to stack conditions inside conditions (nested if)
• How to create clear decision trees with multi-way if-else
• When to use each approach for cleaner code

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a coffee shop with a loyalty program:
- First, you check if you're a member (if statement)
- Then, you check what tier you're in (nested if)
- Finally, you get your discount based on all those conditions

That's exactly how nested if statements work! They let you ask follow-up questions after the first decision.

**Nested if statements** are like Russian nesting dolls - conditions inside conditions:
• First check: Are you a member?
• If yes, check: Gold, Silver, or Bronze tier?
• Then apply the right discount

**Multi-way if-else** is like a game show with multiple doors:
• Door 1: Score > 90 → A grade
• Door 2: Score > 80 → B grade
• Door 3: Score > 70 → C grade
• Default: Try again next time!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Nested if places an if statement inside the body of another if or else
Multi-way if-else (else if chain) tests multiple conditions in sequence
Only the first matching condition's block is executed; the rest are skipped
The final else acts as a default case when no conditions match
Each else pairs with its nearest preceding unmatched if (dangling else rule)

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Nested if lets you ask follow-up questions after a condition is met. Multi-way if-else handles multiple exclusive options cleanly. Always test all possible paths through your conditions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'else if' in a multi-way if-else statement?
options: To check additional conditions when previous conditions are false
questions.explanation: 'else if' allows testing additional conditions when the preceding if/else-if condition is false. It creates a chain of condition checks, with only the first true condition's block executing.

questions.question: In a nested if-else, which if does an else belong to?
options: The first if in the code
It can belong to any if
questions.explanation: In Java, an else clause is associated with the nearest preceding unmatched if statement. This is known as the 'dangling else' rule.
